newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil at 5-yr high, jet fuel stable.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil at 5-yr high, jet fuel stable.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil traded on Friday at a new five-year high on strong regional demand but fuel oil stayed stable, traders said.
A 150,000 barrel gas oil cargo was sold by a European major to a Singapore trader, lifting November 26-30 at $30.60 per barrel, five cents more than a previous record in mid-October.

The same trader bought a second cargo at $30.60 from another major loading in early December and a third from a trader at $30.35 for similar timings. Gas oil prices in Singapore were firm over the past weeks despite falling prices in the west due to strong regional demand.
Jet fuel held steady but is under some selling pressure due to reduced buying from North Asia and high regional stocks.

A 60,000-tonne cargo was sold into South Korea earlier this week for arrival in early December at $1.45 premium to spot Singapore quotes on a cost-and-freight basis, 5-10 cents below the previous deal to Japan.

As a result, the November jet fuel/gas oil swaps spread moved into the negative with buyers backing off to bid at a lower level of -$0.40 facing sellers at flat. On Thursday, November was talked at -$0.10/+$0.20.

The light distillate market was in comparison, lacklustre ahead of the long weekend. Only one buyer emerged in the gasoline market, seeking 50,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded material at $24.90 a barrel fob Singapore. But sellers failed to appear. Naphtha rose with firmer crude and swaps levels. November was bid/asked at $22.05/$22.10 a barrel, up from $21.75/$21.90 on Thursday. Taiwan issued its one-year tender for 1997 for around 30,000 tonees of naphthenic and aromatic material which closes November 18.
Fuel oil prices firmed on strong bids with 180 cst traded at $119.25 a tonne for end November lifting.
